payload.claim: The three commit hashes the Context section cites for the operator's hand amendments — `4d65206a` for DESIGN.md §5.6, `e6880cb0` for DESIGN.md §6, and `ae9c9dc3` for CONTEXT.md's Rebuttal entry — do not resolve to any object in this repository's full history (`git cat-file -t` fails on all three, and the repo is not shallow). This is unlike other short-hash citations of the same style elsewhere in `.saffron/specs/*.md` (e.g. `20adc839`, `30c851cb`, `8b93875c`, `c8e8f6e6`), which do resolve as real commits, so the convention is meant to be a verifiable SHA and these three are not. The substance of the claim is nonetheless true at this snapshot: DESIGN.md already carries the quoted §5.6 text ('An unreadable rebuttal is recorded as unreadable, never as no answer') around line 1291 and the quoted §6 text ('An unread or unanswered blocker ranks with a sustained one too, and keeps its own count') around line 1441, so the spec's authorization basis for the feature stands even though its citation of exactly when/how it was amended is unverifiable. This costs nothing for the operator to leave, since it changes nothing about what the cell would build.
